clues: The world's largest city rings a deep bay on the east coast of a long island nation, backed by mountains and a perfect cone volcano to the west.
Summers are hot, sticky, and lashed by typhoons; winters turn dry and bright as cold winds blow in off the mainland — snow is rare.
A fishing village grew around a warlord's castle from 1603; after 1868 the emperor moved in and the castle town became the nation's capital.
Its dawn fish market once sold more tuna before sunrise than most ports sell all day, and its subway carries more riders daily than some nations' railways.
In the old riverside district stands the city's oldest temple, entered through a gate hung with a giant red paper lantern.
